title.narrative: UNESCO collaborates with and supports the Tanzania Association of Engineers -Women Chapter to organize Tanzania Women Convention and Exhibition in the Framework of the Africa Engineering Week 2024

description.narrative: Science, Technology, and Engineering play a crucial role in transforming many aspects of our lives and offering unprecedented opportunities for all. Women are highly impacted by advancement of technology and challenges such as climate change, yet the gender gap in STEM remains significant. In general, women continue to constitute a minority group in various scientific disciplines; however, the gaps are greatest in engineering and computer science. Globally, women composed only 28% of engineering graduates and 40% of computer science graduates in 2018 (latest available data source UNESCO), while in Tanzania, women engineers constitute 13% of the engineering workforce. As a country, Tanzania needs to ensure that policies and measures are enacted to promote inclusion and diversity in both STEM education and the workforce. This will all, regardless of gender, be provided with the knowledge, skills, and competencies necessary to thrive in these sectors. Additionally, policies must foster long-term opportunities required for STEM career pathways, retaining and working within these fields. It is crucial that our systems leverage the potential benefits of gender inclusion. To this effect, actions that promote equity, diversity and inclusion should be reshaped to meet the needs of sustainable development, ensuring that no one is left behind. The propelling Industrial Revolution and rapid future landscape of the job market, such as AI, necessitate a new perspective and stronger emphasis on the advanced empowerment of women in STEM fields. This aligns with the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which require new approaches towards gender equality, especially in fields where women are underrepresented. The annual event (TAWECE) calls for collaborative efforts among stakeholders to ensure that women play an active in driving more progress towards a sustainable world through inclusive systems. By doing so, we can create a more equitable and sustainable future for all. In the view above UNESCO and Institute of Engineers Tanzania -Women Chapter are collaborating to organize the TAWECE event in the framework of Africa Engineering Week 2024. By engaging in this event UNESCO visibility on its mandate in promotion of women and girls in STEM will be increased through participation in dialogue, Social Media, UNESCO web, local TV shows as preparations for the week and through the Head of Office delivering a key note remarks during the opening session to be attended by the Vice President of the United Republic of Tanzania.
